utterances.text: I did not have a chance to discuss the matter with Mr. Russo. I know he wanted to reserve his position until after the cross-examination. I can talk to him after court today and either then informally Chambers and the parties, or tomorrow morning inform the Chamber of our final position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps that would be a good idea that at least we hear if there are no further objections. If there are any objections we'd like to hear them in court. And if matters go as smoothly as they went today, we might find time tomorrow to deal with this matter as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm much obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have seen that the time estimates today -- that less time was used than one would expect, in view of the time estimates given by the parties. Is there a chance or should I said a risk that the same happens tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, is it your intention to proceed tomorrow as did you today; that is, just to seek the attestations and apart from that not to -- because you announced that you would need half a session. Of course, you used far less than half a session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, my guess is, looking at how long it takes to put into evidence a 92 ter, I've guessed it's about half an hour that one needs clearing everything up by the time we start, so that will be my time with Mr. Skegro. I believe the other witnesses for this week are scheduled to fly tomorrow, so they will be here for Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. I think both of them are coming at the same time. If one goes shorter -- we did have a witness, unfortunately, become unavailable for this week so we've had to move him out of the -- the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. Mr. Hedaraly, I don't know whether you will be the one who will cross-examine the witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I will be. And it will be very likely that it will also -- we will also end earlier tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, at this moment, what remains is to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have two additional matters if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, we've got time now so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yeah. I believe D1465 was something that we were going to get back to, that is the Mladic diary, and the Prosecution needed to take a look at the excerpts we had selected, which are 65 ter 1D2976. Then I have one other procedural matter to address.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes. I must confess I didn't bring my list of outstanding issues. I will have it tomorrow, but on that specific issue, we did review it and there are no objections from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me check my list. Yes. I do understand that we were -- actually, we were waiting for the response by the OTP on admission, which was due on the 25th of September. I do understand that the version that was uploaded as D1465 should be replaced with 1D2976. Has that been done? Because there was a new version, from what I understand. Perhaps a more complete one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it has -- it is in e-court as 65 ter 1D2976, and D1465, I believe, still has MFI status. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- we are just waiting for permission of the Chamber to replace what is currently D1465 MFI, which is the entire diary, with the excerpts, which are 1D2976.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I do understand that the Prosecution has no problems with that. Then the Gotovina is granted leave to replace the present D1465 with 1D2976, and that new D1465 is admitted into evidence. That was one issue -- yes, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: While we're dealing with some issues that I can remember have been advised of, there's also P2563 which at the last housekeeping sessions, Mr. Kehoe had asked to look at it at the break, but I think it fell through the cracks, and it is still MFI P2563. If we could just that as well admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Counsel, if I may, can just remind me what that is. I do believe that subject came up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- with regard to a document that I said I had no objection to but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It a criminal report against an unidentified person who committed rape. That was the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President -- I think, Mr. President, you brought that to my attention last week because you said we were looking for a response, and my objection to that document was based on the admission or non-admission of two other documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- the Chamber admitted in, and then I withdrew my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1551 and D1552 were these other documents, and we did invite the Gotovina Defence to express whether they still had objections once a decision had been taken on these two documents. Since there are no further objections, P2563 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Misetic -- Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's actually -- with regard to one other document, which is D970, and I will bring the documentation with me tomorrow, Mr. President, and it will be very brief. But we could ask the Chamber to assist with CLSS and request the Chamber's intervention on a translation issue, but I was unaware that we were going to do housekeeping work today but I will bring it to Your Honours' attention tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said that we would just deal with some leftovers and not necessarily -- it was not announced as such, but since we had time, we could deal with the matter, and some of these matters had to wait until we had received further submissions which were due either last Friday or by tomorrow. So there's no blame whatsoever for not being fully prepared on this matter at this moment. Mr. Misetic is that -- that was -- that covered the other issue you wanted to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we will adjourn and we will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 29th of September, 9.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of September, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
